author: north vegas times
title: Poll identifies top three short road trips for Nevada families amid rising gas prices
text:
Nevada families are adjusting their summer travel plans as gas prices remain high, according to a June 19 survey by RV Windshield Replacement. The poll of 3,002 experienced road-tripping families highlights the most recommended short road trips in the state, offering alternatives to traditional long-distance vacations.
The survey identified three top routes: Las Vegas to Mt. Charleston via Valley of Fire, Reno to Great Basin National Park via Austin, and Carson City to Ruby Mountains/Lamoille Canyon via Elko. Each route was selected for its ability to provide a classic road trip experience with lower fuel costs, less mileage, and reduced time commitment. The Las Vegas to Mt. Charleston route features a transition from city lights to red rock formations and cooler mountain air. The Reno to Great Basin National Park trip includes stretches of desert and remote scenery, while the Carson City to Ruby Mountains route offers historic sites and alpine landscapes.
The survey found that nearly two-thirds of Nevada families are rethinking their summer road trip plans due to high gas prices. Sixty-eight percent said they are more likely to take a shorter, in-state trip, and 47 percent indicated they would consider inviting another family or relatives to share costs. Eighty-six percent believe that the classic long-distance American road trip is becoming less affordable for ordinary families. When asked about the most expensive aspect of road trips, 67 percent cited gas, followed by hotels, food, attractions, and car maintenance.
Families reported that when budgets are tight, they are most likely to cut souvenirs, the trip itself, restaurant meals, overnight hotel stays, theme parks or attractions, and extra sightseeing stops. The survey also revealed that 26 percent of respondents plan to take the same trip on a tighter budget, 18 percent will stay in-state, 17 percent are proceeding as planned, 16 percent will opt for a shorter drive, 16 percent have canceled their trip, and 10 percent have downgraded their plans. On average, families said gas prices would need to rise by about $0.55 per gallon—reaching $5.70 in Nevada—before they would cancel their summer road trip plans.
“Road trips have always been one of the most flexible ways for families to travel, but this summer that flexibility is being tested. What we’re seeing is not that families have lost their appetite for adventure, but that they are becoming much more strategic about it. Shorter routes, shared costs, fewer overnight stops—these are the new realities for families trying to keep the summer road trip alive without letting fuel prices take the wheel,” according to a spokesperson for RV Windshield Replacement.

The poll of 3,002 experienced road-tripping families highlights the most recommended short road trips in the state, offering alternatives to traditional long-distance vacations. The Reno to Great Basin National Park trip includes stretches of desert and remote scenery, while the Carson City to Ruby Mountains route offers historic sites and alpine landscapes.
